intro: You are in Kastamonu Archaeology Museum, in Kastamonu province, founded in 1943. Here finds from the rock tombs of Paphlagonia and the Pompeiopolis excavation are gathered — in the very hall where Atatürk announced the hat reform.
history: The museum was founded in 1943 in a building put up in the Republic's first years. Its collection comes from the rock tombs of Paphlagonia and from the Pompeiopolis excavation. But the building has its own story too: in 1925, Atatürk announced the hat reform in this hall.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Paphlagonian finds and the material from Pompeiopolis, then the hall of the hat reform and the ethnography section.
facts: Did you know? The Paphlagonian rock tombs, with temple fronts cut into the cliff, resemble those of Lycia — yet no connection between the two regions is known. And it was in the hall of this very building that Atatürk announced the hat reform in 1925.
outro: This brings our journey through Kastamonu Archaeology Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Let these treasures stay bright for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
